'''Govind P. Agrawal''' is an [[Indian Americans|Indian American]] physicist and a fellow of Optica, Life Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]], and Distinguished Fellow of the Optical Society of India. He is the recipient of James C. Wyant Professorship of Optics at the [[The Institute of Optics|Institute of Optics]] and a professor of physics at the [[University of Rochester]]. He is also a Distinguished scientist at the [[Laboratory for Laser Energetics]] (LLE) in the University of Rochester. Agrawal has authored and co-authored several highly cited books in the fields of non-linear [[Optical fiber|fiber optics]], [[optical communication]]s, and [[Laser diode|semiconductor lasers]].

== Early life ==
Agrawal was born on July 24, 1951, in [[Kashipur, Uttarakhand|Kashipur]] of the [[Nainital district]], which was then a part of [[Uttar Pradesh]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|url=https://www.elsevier.com/books/nonlinear-fiber-optics/agrawal/978-0-12-397023-7|title=Nonlinear Fiber Optics - 5th Edition|last=Elsevier|website=www.elsevier.com|date=10 October 2012 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-397023-7 |language=en|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> He received the [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in physics degree from the [[University of Lucknow]] in 1969, with honors. He received the [[Master of Science|M.S.]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics degrees from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Delhi]], in 1971 and 1974 respectively.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www2.optics.rochester.edu/users/gpa/BIO.htm|title=Resume|website=www2.optics.rochester.edu|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> He worked in a post-doctoral position in [[École polytechnique]] in [[France]], from 1974 to 1976.<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
From 1977 to 1979, Agrawal worked as a research associate at the [[City University of New York]]. During 1980 and 1981 he worked with the company Quantel, in France.<ref name=":2" /> Later, he was a member of technical staff at the [[AT&T Bell Laboratories]] in [[Murray Hill, New Jersey]], where he worked from 1982 to 1988 on [[Laser diode|semiconductor lasers]] and nonlinear fiber optics.<ref name=":1" />

Agrawal joined University of Rochester in 1989 as a Professor of Optics. In 2013, he received the first Dr. James C. Wyant Professorship in Optics in the [[The Institute of Optics|Institute of Optics]], which was established by [[James C. Wyant]] himself.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.azooptics.com/News.aspx?newsID=18200|title=Dr. James C. Wyant Professorship in Optics Bestowed on Distinguished Researcher, Govind Agarwal|date=2013-11-21|website=AZoOptics.com|language=en|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> From 2008 to 2013, Agrawal served on the Editorial Advisory Board,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2008/editorialadvisor/|title=OSA's Review Journal Advances in Optics and Photonics Announces Editorial Advisory Board|last=|first=|date=|website=Optical Society of America|access-date=}}</ref> and from 2014 to 2020, he was the Editor-in-Chief of the Advances in Optics and Photonics Journal of Optical Society of America.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.osapublishing.org/aop/journal/aop/about.cfm|title=OSA {{!}} About Advances in Optics and Photonics|website=www.osapublishing.org|language=en|access-date=2021-12-16}}</ref> According to Agrawal, his research interest shifted from [[telecommunication]]s to [[silicon photonics]] in 2000, due to [[Dot-com bubble#Bubble in telecom|telecommunications bubble]] burst.<ref name=":1" /> After 2010, Agrawal's research focused on temporal waveguides, [[graded-index fiber]]s, and [[optical communication]]s.

== Awards ==
Agrawal was elected as the fellow of [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA) in 1986.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/100/osa_stories/govind_agrawal/|title=Govind Agrawal|last=|first=|date=|website=Optical Society of America|access-date=}}</ref> In 1996, he was elected as the [[IEEE Fellow|fellow of IEEE]] for "contributions to the development and understanding of semiconductor lasers and fiber-optic communications systems."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=38r3OqiDvx8e861ATUOc2A==&bccaptions=Search%20Results&bclocations=/fellowsdirectory/keywordsearch.html?keyword=Govind|title=IEEE Fellows Directory - Member Profile|website=[[IEEE]]|language=en|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> In 2000, he was awarded the Distinguished Alumni Award by his alma mater, the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. In 2012, Agrawal was awarded the [[Quantum Electronics Award]] by the [[IEEE Photonics Society]] for "sustained contributions to fiber-optic telecommunication technology through innovative research and authorship of numerous widely-respected books in the field". Agrawal was awarded the William H. Riker University Award for Graduate Teaching from the [[University of Rochester]] in 2013, during the commencement ceremony. In 2015, he was awarded the [[Esther Hoffman Beller Medal]] by the [[Optical Society]] for "inspiring and educating a generation of scientists and engineers involved with fiber-optic communications and other photonics technologies through his seminal textbooks and high-impact scientific articles".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2015/the_optical_society_bestows_fifteen_prestigious_aw/|title=The Optical Society Bestows Fifteen Prestigious Awards for 2015|last=|first=|date=|website=Optical Society of America|access-date=}}</ref> Agrawal was the recipient of two major awards in 2019: [[Max Born Award]] of the [[Optical Society]] and the Quantum Electronics Prize of the [[European Physical Society]]. He was given in 2020 the Lifetime Achievement Award by the Hajim School of Engineering of [[University of Rochester]].

== Publications ==
Agrawal has authored or co-authored more than 500 research papers in internationally reputed scientific journals and has made more than 200 conference presentations. He has also published 10 books. Most of his publications are highly cited.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=StqcycAAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Prof. Govind P. Agrawal - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.co.in|access-date=2018-11-16}}</ref> His book ''Nonlinear Fiber Optics,'' first published in 1989, is now in its sixth edition and has also been translated into several languages. Another book ''Fiber-Optic Communication Systems,'' first published in 1992 and currently in its fifth edition, is used as a standard textbook in many universities for courses on telecommunication. The list of books published by Agrawal is as follows.

# G. P. Agrawal and N. K. Dutta, [[Semiconductor Lasers]], 2nd ed. (Springer, 2002).
# Yu. S. Kivshar and G. P. Agrawal, [[Optical Solitons: From Fibers to Photonic Crystals]] (Academic Press, 2003).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Lightwave Technology: Components and Devices]] (Wiley, 2004).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Lightwave Technology: Telecommunication Systems]] (Wiley, 2005).
# M. Premaratne and G. P. Agrawal, [[Light Propagation in Gain Media: Optical Amplifiers]] (Cambridge University Press, 2011).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Nonlinear Fiber Optics]], 6th ed. (Academic Press, 2019).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Applications of Nonlinear Fiber Optics]], 3rd ed (Academic Press, 2020).
# M. Premaratne and G. P. Agrawal, [[Theoretical Foundations of Nanoscale Quantum Devices]] (Cambridge University Press, 2021).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Fiber-Optic Communication Systems]], 5th ed. (Wiley, 2021).
# G. P. Agrawal, [[Physics and Engineering of Graded-Index Media]] (Cambridge University Press, 2023).
